claim_verdicts.evidence: AuthController.Login @ stage-1 only reads db.Customers (FirstOrDefaultAsync), then 'return Ok(new LoginResponse(token))' - no write, no SaveChanges. Program.cs: AddJwtBearer + UseAuthentication. ASP.NET Core docs: 'The JwtBearerHandler validates the token and extracts the user's identity from its claims.' Run: same token -> GET /api/v1/orders 200; no header -> 401. The api log line for login is only 'POST /api/v1/auth/login responded 200' (no identity).

Lab run via Caddy :8080: correct password -> 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK', 'Content-Type: application/json', body '{"token":"eyJ..."}' (single field). Wrong password -> 'HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized', application/problem+json {type,title,status,traceId}, no token. Unknown email nobody@example.com -> 'HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized'. Code: 'return Unauthorized();' / 'Ok(new LoginResponse(token))'; Dtos.cs 'record LoginResponse(string Token)'.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Dart SDK (Flutter 3.47.2) core/exceptions.dart class _Exception: 'if (message == null) return "Exception"; return "Exception: $message";'. Execution: headless Chrome, wrong password on the lab app -> semantics node text 'Exception: login failed (401)'.

Flutter 3.47.2 framework.dart: 'Whether this [State] object is currently in a tree. ... The [State] object remains mounted until the framework calls [dispose]'. Flutter docs guidance: 'After an asynchronous gap, check mounted in a State ... before calling setState, using the context, or doing other work that requires the State to remain in the tree.' mounted means 'still in the tree', not 'still showing' (a State under a covering route is mounted but not visible).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: The `mounted` check before that makes sure the screen is still in the widget tree after the wait (the user may have left it with Back), since `context` belongs to it.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Security principle / design consequence (more copies = more exposure; a 401 must surface to the user), consistent with outline item 3 and misconception 2; no version-dependent behavior asserted. Lesson wording has no 'always/never' beyond what it reasons from.

issues.text: Try-it step 2 says to pick 'the POST one, if two are listed', implying only one POST. After step 1 the Network tab already holds a POST login with 401 (Problem Details body); step 2 adds another POST with 200 (plus an OPTIONS preflight). Verified in headless Chrome: POST 401, OPTIONS 204, POST 200. A learner who opens the first POST sees type/title/status JSON, not the expected single token field.
issues.quote: select the `login` request (the `POST` one, if two are listed) and open its response

issues.text: State.mounted means the State is still in the tree (until dispose), not that the screen is 'still showing'. A mounted State can be hidden under another route. The code is right; the prose overstates what the check tests.
issues.quote: The `mounted` check before that makes sure the screen is still showing after the wait, since `context` belongs to it.
